label: Event type
description: Something that happens in the workspace that other parts of the platform can react to, such as "Ticket escalated". Modules and tenants declare the events they publish with a small payload; notifications, alerts, automations and integrations subscribe to them by ID, so the publisher never needs to know who listens. Transitions publish events with emits, and rules with an emit_event action when their condition becomes true.
usage: Name events after what happened, in the past tense: <module>.<entity>.<what_happened>, e.g. core.tickets.ticket.escalated.
Keep payloads small: IDs, choice IDs, numbers and flags; subscribers read the record for everything else under their own permissions.
Set a default severity, and compute a different one where it matters (e.g. critical for P1).
constraints: id is unique; tenant event types start with tenant__.
version starts at 1; a breaking payload change publishes version + 1.
Payload field keys are snake_case with type string, number, boolean or list; at most 30 fields.
severity is info, low, medium, high or critical; sensitivity is public, internal or restricted (external recipients only ever get public values).
Emitters must set every required field and only declared fields; their expressions are type-checked.
